system.summary: A source-linked pilot dossier for the DS200 within the EAC-certified EVS 6.4.0.0 configuration, with historical change records, separately scoped optional modem models and vulnerability reviews, and a labeled Washington deployment observation.

certification.caveat: EAC certification applies only to the evaluated EVS 6.4.0.0 certified configuration. It is not an endorsement, warranty, field inventory, or determination that a particular unit was operated in that configuration.

components.name: DS200 scanner and tabulator assembly
components.description: The certified scope describes the DS200 as a poll-place scanner and tabulator that scans voter selections from both sides of a ballot simultaneously.
components.caveat: Washington's state-approved configuration also lists hardware 1.3.13. No source in this pilot identifies the hardware revision of a particular county unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Cellular modem
technicalSpecifications.value: No WAN modem or WAN wireless use listed in the EVS 6.4.0.0 certified-system table
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is a certified-system communications-use statement. It does not prove the physical absence of every connector or service component inside every DS200 unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Ethernet / LAN
technicalSpecifications.value: No LAN TCP/IP or LAN wireless use listed in the EVS 6.4.0.0 certified-system table
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This establishes permitted certified-system communications use, not a teardown-based count of physical RJ-45 connectors.

technicalSpecifications.label: Physical USB port count
technicalSpecifications.caveat: Reviewed certification artifacts identify removable media and system components but do not publish a DS200 physical USB-connector count.

technicalSpecifications.label: Installed RAM
technicalSpecifications.caveat: No reviewed artifact publishes the installed RAM technology or capacity for the certified DS200 configurations.

components.name: Optional modem carrier board
components.description: ES&S states that modem components are not resident by default and that a separate board is installed only where cellular transmission is permitted; Rhode Island's 2021 procedure documents post-poll cellular transmission. Exact historical modem modules are listed as separate evidence records below.
components.caveat: The sources establish an optional separate board and one jurisdiction's documented procedure, but not this carrier board's manufacturer, part number, radio module, firmware, antenna, exact placement, or presence in every DS200. The scene shape is symbolic.

technicalSpecifications.label: Optional cellular transmission
technicalSpecifications.value: Separate modem board installed only where permitted; Rhode Island documents transmission after polls close
technicalSpecifications.modelContext: DS200 model family; Rhode Island 2021 deployment procedure
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This does not mean every DS200 contains a modem, that EVS 6.4.0.0 permits WAN use, or that cellular transmission was enabled or used in an unlisted jurisdiction.

securityReview.coverageDefinition: All publicly indexed, exact-product-applicable records found in the reviewed NVD, CISA KEV, and manufacturer security-advisory sources as of the review date.
securityReview.rankingMethod: Known exploitation in CISA KEV ranks first, then numeric CVSS score, then a source-assigned severity. No score or severity is invented when a source does not publish one.
securityReview.caveat: An exact-product vulnerability review cannot be performed until the carrier board and installed modem module are identified. An empty list here is an evidence gap, not a claim of no vulnerabilities.

components.name: MultiTech Verizon C2 cellular modem
components.description: Florida's June 2015 qualification addendum identifies a MultiTech Verizon C2 modem evaluated as an optional DS200 result-transmission component.
components.caveat: This model is established only for Florida EVS 4.5.0.0 Version 4 and DS200 hardware 1.2 or 1.3. The public record does not establish EVS 6.4.0.0 certification, Rhode Island fielding, a current installed unit, radio firmware, antenna installation, or exact internal placement.

technicalSpecifications.label: Carrier and radio family
technicalSpecifications.modelContext: Florida EVS 4.5.0.0 Version 4; DS200 hardware 1.2 and 1.3
technicalSpecifications.caveat: This is a historical state-approved configuration, not proof that a modem was installed or enabled in another DS200 configuration or jurisdiction.

technicalSpecifications.label: Documented firmware update path
technicalSpecifications.value: Non-UIP C2 SocketModem firmware can be updated through the serial port with MultiTech assistance
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The guide describes an update method, not the firmware version installed in the Florida test modem or any fielded DS200.

nonCveAdvisories.title: Verizon LTE Cat 1 software patch bulletin
nonCveAdvisories.description: MultiTech reported an urgent software-patch need for listed Verizon LTE Cat 1 products, possibly including MTSMC-LVW3 variants, to support future network updates and uninterrupted operation.
nonCveAdvisories.caveat: The bulletin is not a CVE or security advisory, assigns no CVSS score, and does not establish the firmware or patch state of the Pro V&V DS200 test modems or any fielded unit.

components.name: Ballot scanning path
components.description: The public certification scope establishes simultaneous front-and-back ballot scanning. The schematic path is illustrative and does not reproduce proprietary internal drawings.
components.caveat: Public sources document the function, not the exact internal shape or placement shown in the schematic.

components.name: Display and touchscreen assembly
components.description: ECO 1042 identifies a touchscreen controller, LCD, mounting bracket, LVDS cables, and a field-service display subassembly in DS200 hardware configuration 1.3.11.
components.caveat: This historical ECO identifies a DS200-family configuration change. It does not prove that the illustrated assembly is present in an EVS 6.4.0.0 fielded unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Processor architecture
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The approved change identifies the core count but not the processor manufacturer, model, clock speed, or the configuration of a particular fielded unit.

technicalSpecifications.label: Exact CPU model
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The reviewed ECO analysis does not name an exact processor part number.

components.name: Processor module
components.description: ECO 1042 records a move to a quad-core processor on the motherboard for DS200 hardware configuration 1.3.11.
components.caveat: Processor make, model, location, and presence in a particular EVS 6.4.0.0 fielded unit are not publicly confirmed by this pilot.

components.name: Scanner board and FPGA logic
components.description: ECO 1035 documents a DS200 scanner-board FPGA-code update intended to improve thermal stability and calibration resolution; ECO 1042 also references a board change for a new motor driver.
components.caveat: The public records do not identify a board part number or establish the board/FPGA revision installed in a particular EVS 6.4.0.0 unit.

components.name: Ballot container options
components.description: The EVS 6.4.0.0 scope lists multiple DS200/DS300-compatible ballot boxes, tote bins, a trolley, tote bag, and carrying cases as proprietary configuration components.
components.caveat: These are permitted configuration options, not a claim that every DS200 uses every listed container or accessory.

components.name: Tote-bin security gasketing
components.description: ECO 1165 adds a security gasketing kit intended to prevent cards or ballots from entering through gaps along the tote-bin hinge area.
components.caveat: The change was approved for EVS 6.4.0.0, but the pilot has no evidence that a particular jurisdiction installed the kit.

components.name: Exterior seal area
components.description: ECO 983 documents a historical DS200 hardware 1.3.10.0 exterior seal-area change.
components.caveat: This record does not establish inclusion in EVS 6.4.0.0 or installation on any fielded unit.

components.name: Battery backup and internal power
components.description: The ES&S one-sheet states that the DS200 has battery backup. The reviewed sources do not identify its battery chemistry, manufacturer, model, capacity, runtime, or internal placement.
components.caveat: Battery-backup presence is manufacturer-documented, but no reviewed source supports a battery model, capacity, runtime, chemistry, or scene placement. Central-count UPS models must not be transferred to the DS200.

technicalSpecifications.label: Backup supply
technicalSpecifications.value: Battery backup documented; model, chemistry, capacity, and runtime not stated
technicalSpecifications.caveat: The one-sheet confirms battery-backup presence only. It does not disclose a battery part number or unit-level condition.

configurationChanges.caveat: The ECO documents an approved historical configuration change, not the internals of every DS200 or an EVS 6.4.0.0 deployment.

findings.title: Pro V&V anomaly status
findings.description: The certification test report states that no anomalies occurred during the EVS 6.4.0.0 test campaign.
findings.caveat: This is scoped to the submitted test campaign. It is not a claim that the system has no bugs or that no field incident can occur.

findings.title: Deficiencies described but not itemized
findings.description: The public report says encountered deficiencies were tracked and resolutions verified as needed, but section 3.3 does not itemize those deficiencies.
findings.caveat: Do not infer the number, severity, affected component, or field impact of non-enumerated test deficiencies.

findings.title: Previously scanned ballot is not automatically distinguished
findings.description: Washington's staff report states that EVS 6.4.0.0 cannot distinguish whether a ballot was previously scanned and describes ballot-handling and staffing controls recommended by ES&S.
findings.caveat: This is an operational limitation and mitigation note, not evidence that duplicate scanning occurred in an election.

findings.title: No advisory attachment listed on selected EAC record
findings.description: The archived EAC EVS 6.4.0.0 record did not list an advisory attachment when retrieved on 2026-07-19.
findings.caveat: This is a page-listing observation, not a claim that no advisories, bugs, vulnerabilities, service bulletins, or field incidents exist.

power.description: The ES&S one-sheet confirms DS200 battery backup. The certification and state records reviewed here do not publish the battery manufacturer, model, chemistry, capacity, runtime, condition, or jurisdiction power topology.
power.caveat: Confirmed battery-backup presence must not be expanded into an inferred model, runtime, internal location, service condition, or claim about external site power.

networkEvidence.summary: For EVS 6.4.0.0, the EAC scope defines Regional Results as a separate application at a regional sending site, and Pro V&V tested transmission of DS200 result files through Regional Results over a VPN. The reviewed exact-version text does not establish that the DS200 itself was the VPN endpoint. Older records separately document optional DS200 cellular hardware families without proving EVS 6.4 certification, firmware, activation, or field use.
networkEvidence.publicationBoundary: The module publishes roles, high-level paths, connection media when established, and evidence boundaries. It excludes IP addresses, credentials, VPN parameters, keys, APNs, SIM identifiers, carrier accounts, device identifiers, and jurisdiction routing details.

caveats: Certified configuration is not the same as field deployment. A county system-version record does not establish the components, firmware, hardware revision, or change orders installed on each unit.
The photo-informed 3D schematic is a selection aid, not vendor CAD, a teardown, an engineering drawing, or proof of exact dimensions or internal placement.

Public findings and modem vulnerability reviews are presented with exact product, firmware, date, and source scope. A zero-match catalog review is not evidence that no bug, vulnerability, incident, or service bulletin exists.
The manufacturer documents DS200 battery backup, but its model, chemistry, capacity, runtime, internal placement, condition, and county-level power topology remain unknown.
